dimensions.reasons: The submitted view retains the broad reference staging grammar: a school of orange-toned fish occupies the middle, rocks and pale substrate sit below, a dark branch arcs from the left, a dense plant cluster fills the right, and the scene is blue lit (Group A wide_front; Group C frame_0001).
issues: The fish are highly simplified, nearly identical peach fish rather than the varied orange, red-orange, gold, and white goldfish in the reference.
The reference's prominent large upper-right fish, forward-facing center fish, and cropped lower-right fish are not convincingly recreated.
The bright flat-blue background and oversized plant mass differ substantially from the darker, more natural aquarium framing.

dimensions.reasons: The rocks and plant stems generally meet the floor, and the fish plausibly float in the water volume. However, Group A detail_environment and wide_front clearly show many planar fins and leaves, fish passing into the right plant cluster, and disconnected rod-like branch pieces.
issues: Fish tails, fins, and plant leaves are visibly paper-thin planes with no credible thickness.
Several fish, tails, stems, and leaves visibly interpenetrate, especially at the dense right plant cluster.
Some driftwood/branch segments terminate abruptly or hang unsupported.
There is no coherent visible tank enclosure or water-surface boundary; the environment opens onto a flat backdrop.

dimensions.reasons: The fish read independently as fish because of their oval bodies, fins, tails, and eyes, and the blue-green aquarium palette is recognizable. Group A detail_hero also shows that the bodies have a surface texture rather than being featureless primitives.
issues: The fish are mostly the same muted peach/tan color instead of the reference's varied orange, red-orange, gold, and white coloration.
Oversized glossy black spherical eyes and simple triangular fins give the fish a toy-like silhouette rather than a goldfish appearance.
The large pale fork tails are rigid flat sheets rather than translucent, naturally shaped goldfish tails.
The right-hand plant uses narrow flat strips rather than the reference plant's fuller pointed oval leaves.

dimensions.reasons: The Group C frames are cleanly rendered and have readable foreground, middle-ground, and background layers, but the combined image remains overtly low-detail and artificial rather than a believable aquarium.
issues: Rigid identical fish, giant eyes, and planar transparent tails undermine biological believability.
The crowded plant/fish intersections and floating branch fragments make the scene visibly constructed rather than natural.
The background is a very bright, smooth blue field with simple dark wave-like forms rather than the reference's subdued underwater rocky depth.
The faceted rocks, flat leaves, and coarse fish texture do not integrate into a coherent natural material style.

dimensions.reasons: The key broad spatial relationships are present: bottom rocks and substrate, fish crossing the central water space, driftwood framing the left/upper area, and a dense green plant group on the right (Group A wide_front). The Group C sequence also shows fish changing position through the layered scene from frame_0001 to frame_0016.
issues: Nearly all visible fish face in the same horizontal direction, unlike the varied crossing and forward-facing poses in the reference.
The submitted fish form an even, rigid school instead of the reference's strongly varied foreground/background size and position arrangement.
The dense right-side foliage obscures and intersects fish rather than serving as a clear background edge decoration.
The central foreground is dominated by a large isolated dome rock, unlike the reference's more irregular clustered rock arrangement.

dimensions.reasons: Fish, plants, and rocks are all visible at aquarium-like scales, and Group C frame_0001 provides some depth through a larger nearer fish and smaller rear fish.
issues: The fish are too uniform in body size despite the reference's clear large, medium, small, foreground, and cropped fish hierarchy.
Tails are disproportionately broad and nearly body-length, dominating several frames.
The eyes are dramatically oversized for goldfish anatomy.
Large foreground rocks and the extremely tall right-side plant mass compete with rather than support the fish scale hierarchy.

dimensions.reasons: A strong underwater blue illumination is consistently present, and the scene has darker rocks, lightly textured fish bodies, translucent tail planes, and visible bubbles (Group A detail_environment; Group C frame_0008).
issues: The blue illumination is overly even and bright compared with the darker, deeper blue aquarium reference.
Fish materials do not convey orange/gold scale variation, soft flesh, or translucent fin structure convincingly.
Tail transparency exposes the flat construction rather than reading as thin organic membrane.
Rocks and plants have very simple, mostly matte low-poly materials with little natural surface variation.

dimensions.reasons: Most major visible reference inventory is included: roughly the requested number of fish, plants, driftwood-like branches, dark rocks, a pale floor, blue background lighting, and bubbles are all visible in Group A wide_front and Group C frame_0001.
issues: There are six similarly modeled fish rather than the reference's five individually distinct fish.
The specific red-and-white, orange-and-white, and gold fish variations from the reference are absent.
The driftwood is represented by incomplete-looking rods rather than one convincing connected decorative wood structure.
No clear aquarium boundary or surrounding tank structure is visible.

criteria.criterion: The aquarium contains multiple recognizable orange goldfish with reference-like principal anatomy.
criteria.evidence: Several peach-orange stylized fish are clearly visible with volumetric oval bodies, head ends, oversized dark eyes, paired small fins, and large forked tails.

criteria.criterion: The fish group shows reference-like variation in relative size, body proportions, and tail form.
criteria.evidence: The visible fish use essentially the same elongated oval body and the same broad, pale forked tail construction; no clearly round-bodied fish or distinctly different tail forms are shown.

criteria.criterion: Visible underwater bubbles are integrated into the aquarium.
criteria.evidence: Numerous small translucent spherical bubbles are visible throughout the upper and middle water space and remain present across the animation frames.

criteria.criterion: The tank contains the reference-defining plants, branching driftwood, dark rocks, and pale substrate.
criteria.evidence: Plants and dark rocks are clear, but the bottom reads as a light-blue textured ground plane rather than unambiguously sandy/gravelly substrate, and the dark branch elements are only ambiguously recognizable as coherent driftwood.

criteria.criterion: The principal environmental components follow the reference arrangement.
criteria.evidence: A thick dark branching form rises from the left and arcs through the upper center, a tall dense green plant mass occupies the right, and dark rocks sit on the pale floor beneath the fish.

criteria.criterion: Fish occupy distinct depth planes and create readable foreground/background layering.
criteria.evidence: The sequence shows a very large lower foreground fish, smaller rear swimmers around the central background ridge, and partially plant-occluded right-side fish; their screen overlaps shift as the shot progresses.

criteria.criterion: The fish group has the close reference view's prominent central scale, occupancy, and overlap density.
criteria.evidence: Multiple large fish span the middle of the delivered frames, including overlapping central and lower foreground bodies plus further fish partially hidden at right, creating a dense close-view group.

criteria.criterion: The fish reproduce the reference's varied orange and gold coloration, lighter markings, wet bodies, and softer translucent fins.
criteria.evidence: The fish are predominantly a uniform peach/tan treatment with similar surface texture. They lack the reference's clearly differentiated red-orange, gold, and white markings, while the fins and tails read as rigid, paper-thin translucent planes.

criteria.criterion: Plant, driftwood, rock, and substrate materials retain the reference's distinct color and surface character.
criteria.evidence: Although green leaves and dark rocks are visible, the branch forms are smooth dark rods rather than textured driftwood and the light-blue floor does not clearly read as sandy or gravelly substrate.

criteria.criterion: The scene has a strong reference-like underwater blue lighting and atmospheric treatment.
criteria.evidence: Cool cyan-blue illumination dominates every frame, with blue-shaded fish undersides, dark blue receding ridge surfaces, and lighter blue water/background space.

criteria.criterion: Every visible fish remains practically poseable through a usable editable setup in the Blender project.
Fish swimming is visibly propelled by repeated lateral tail strokes.
criteria.evidence: Across the sampled sequence, the large flat forked tails retain nearly the same orientation relative to their fish bodies; no repeated side-to-side tail-beat cycle is clearly readable.

criteria.criterion: Multiple fish perform passes that change their relative positions and overlaps.
criteria.evidence: The sampled frames mainly show a slow continuous camera shift with fish maintaining broadly similar side-by-side relationships; there is no clear multi-fish crossing that visibly changes group occlusions.

criteria.criterion: The broad ordering and pace of major fish turns, passes, and foreground crossings follow the reference.
criteria.evidence: All clearly readable fish remain largely in similar right-facing side profiles throughout the sequence. The reference-like series of turns and pronounced later foreground crossings is not visibly established.

criteria.criterion: The composition reproduces the reference's close aquarium view and readable principal anchors.
criteria.evidence: The delivered camera view is substantially straight-on and close to the school, with a central fish grouping framed by the large left-side branching form and dense tall plant at right.

criteria.criterion: Camera behavior matches the reference's restrained continuous close view.
criteria.evidence: The animation frames show one uninterrupted, gently drifting close shot: environmental elements shift smoothly across frame with no cuts, abrupt zooms, shake, or dramatic orbit.

criteria.criterion: The submitted content render has the requested format, encoding, dimensions, frame rate, and source-like duration.
The delivered .blend is an editable source project containing the recreated scene and animation.

notes: The submission is clearly recognizable as a blue-lit aquarium with multiple fish and the required broad decorations. It captures the general left-driftwood/right-plant composition and shows positional movement across the sampled animation frames, but it falls well short of the reference's natural goldfish anatomy, varied fish staging, believable tail-driven motion, and cohesive underwater realism.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
